candidate.hypothesis: A fresh finite liquid slug released above a fixed, deep receiving basin will produce a reproducible gravity-drop, receiver-contact, retention/spill allocation, and terminal destination event without a moving cup, an internal crest, or an underflow aperture.
candidate.physical_question: Does receiver lateral placement control capture versus spill of a falling liquid slug while the fixed outer tank and receiver remain geometrically intact?
scientific_difference: The liquid source is a free-falling slug with prescribed initial downward velocity; no prescribed wall motion or rotating cup is used.
The receiving object is a raised, finite, open-top basin with a closed floor and side walls; it has no crest crossing and no submerged aperture.
The q axis moves only the stationary receiver centerline in y, exposing centered capture and controlled partial capture at one fixed source state.
The event is source-to-receiver contact followed by retained-versus-spilled destination allocation, rather than moving-cup settling or reservoir underflow.
selection_reason: The existing F2 airborne-slug probes completed solver windows with 0.9885714286, 0.9942857143, and 1.0 identity retention, demonstrating that the transfer/catch observation path is executable at low cost.

The W04 calibration measured pre-impact ballistic center-of-mass error of 0.0186 dp for the existing F2 airborne liquid slug, supporting the gravity/trajectory portion of the mechanism within a stated limited range.
The new basin adds a physical receiver and a finite destination contract, directly addressing the old probe warning that fewer than 500 particles was plumbing evidence only.
The route avoids the known moving-cup ID-loss line, static-hold plume line, receiver/weir hard failure, H2 mDBC static failure, and all submerged-orifice remediation inputs.

no receiver-overflow-weir geometry, generated asset, or terminal matrix reuse
no moving-cup DBC/mDBC input, side-wet canary, or static full-cup input reuse
no same-input retry under a new label, threshold relaxation, early horizon extension, or survivor renormalization
no CPU/native preflight, solver, GPU, queue, ledger, registry, or matrix action from this proposal

construction.definition_policy: After root approval, author a literal new Definition from this geometry contract; do not copy any old F2 XML and then relabel it.

fresh_input_contract.allowed_reference_role: Read-only evidence for mechanism selection and failure comparison. No old generated input, native binary, solver trajectory, or output identity may enter the new scope.

denominator_policy: The 15 rows are fixed at proposal creation and all rows remain in the denominator.
CPU/native preflight, root-review anchor, and structural artifacts receive zero T1 credit.
Solver failure, hard-integrity failure, event censoring, or missing output stays as a zero-credit row.
No same-input retry, threshold relaxation, early extension, or survivor renormalization is allowed.

hard_integrity: native fluid IDs are unique and no active fluid identity is missing
all active position, velocity, density, and mass values are finite
zero closed outer-tank endpoint violations and zero saved chord crossings
zero closed receiver-basin endpoint violations and zero saved chord crossings
zero valid fluid particles outside the explicit runtime domain
native initial mass and full-window mass change satisfy the fixed mass gates

event.drop: the source fluid COM descends into the receiver-height band under gravity before terminal classification
event.receiver_contact: at least 1% of initial native fluid mass enters the one-dp-clear receiver interior
event.destination_allocation: after contact, receiver/interior and outer-tank residual fractions sum to at least 95% of initial mass for 0.20 s; allocation is reported as retained, residual, or spill
event.completion: hard integrity, receiver contact, destination allocation, and full registered window are all observed
event.right_censor_policy: event censoring remains a failed denominator row; one whole-scope extension is allowed only after a complete hard pass and never before root approval

observer_contract_draft.observer_ownership: fixed receiver and outer-tank faces use world coordinates; open top ownership is separate from closed-face endpoint/chord checks; missing IDs never become spill mass

root_review_only_contract.current_action: review proposal and dependency hashes only
root_review_only_contract.step_1: Root reviews that the falling-slug plus fixed-basin topology is a new F2 mechanism and is not a relabelled submerged-orifice, weir, side-wet moving-cup, or static-full-cup input.
root_review_only_contract.step_2: If accepted, root authorizes one fresh literal Definition and one new output namespace for CPU/native preflight; this proposal itself does not authorize either action.
root_review_only_contract.step_3: A separate root receipt must inspect the new Definition hash and authorize exactly one CPU/native preflight; any hard input failure stops the scope and preserves all 15 rows.
root_review_only_contract.step_4: Only a fresh CPU/native pass plus a second root review may authorize one protected solver canary at q=0.5, dp=0.0075; that canary is zero credit and outside the numerator until independently registered.
root_review_only_contract.step_5: Only after protected evidence can root decide whether to materialize the same frozen 15-row plan; full 15-row hard/event completion and Core evaluation remain required for any T1 claim.
